ai.title: An AI assistant that actually operates the shop
ai.intro: You can talk to your shop the way you would talk to an assistant who never gets bored: ask what needs attention this morning, hand over the supplier invoice, tell it to process a return. Most "AI for e-commerce" is a chatbot bolted onto the storefront to answer customer questions, and this is the opposite. Your store exposes itself as a set of tools over the Model Context Protocol, so Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP-capable assistant can read and change real data, with your permissions, your audit trail, and your approval on anything destructive.
ai.asksTitle: Things you can just ask for
asks: Which products sold worst last month and still have stock sitting in the warehouse?
Add these 12 items from the supplier invoice, translate the descriptions, and leave them unpublished.
Put 15% off everything in the Filaments category until Sunday.
What did we actually earn in March after cost of goods and delivery?
Find every product with a missing photo, no category, or a price below cost.
Order #6162 is coming back. Refund it and put the stock back in the store.

chat.title: into.ge admin · MCP

turns.text: Anything above max stock that has not sold since spring — put it on 20% off until Sunday and feature it on the homepage.

32 items sit above their maximum level, and 14 of those have not sold since May.
−20% on those 14 until Sunday, and they are now the “Clearance” row on the homepage. The other 18 still move, so I left their price alone.
Take this supplier page — pull the description and the photos and make it a product in my shop, all four languages.
read supplier page · create_product · attach_product_image ×6 · import_product_specs · translate_text ×12

Description and 6 photos pulled in, written as a draft in Georgian, English, Ukrainian and Russian.
The spec table off that page became filterable attributes. Left unpublished with the price blank — that part is yours.
QIDI raised their prices 8%. Update ours, but back up first.

Backup taken, then 29 QIDI products repriced +8%.
Two were already selling below cost, so I left those and listed them for you. One click restores the backup if you change your mind.
Every morning, message me on Telegram whatever dropped below the reorder point overnight.

Wired to your Telegram. Today it would have said: 269 items below the reorder point, 249 of them at zero.
Want it grouped by supplier so it doubles as the purchase order?
If a customer asks their own ChatGPT for PETG, does my shop show up?

It does. Four PETG lines come back, three of them in stock, with prices, photos and links to your product pages.
The public server only ever sees the catalogue — orders, costs and customers stay on the admin side.

audit.title: A real answer, from the real store
audit.intro: Asked of into.ge's live catalog while writing this page. I didn't pick a flattering question either: it found problems in the shop I run, which is rather the point.
audit.question: Audit the catalog. Anything broken, mislinked or unpublishable?
findings: 17 published products tracking stock with no inventory item linked
158 links whose product and stock-item names don't match, e.g. "ABS-Like OdorLite" → "eResine ABS Odor Grey"
0 missing translations, missing images, empty categories, bad prices, duplicate barcodes or duplicate SKUs
0 orphaned translation rows, shared stock items or links to retired items
audit.footnote: Thirteen classes of defect, checked across the whole catalog in one question. Finding the same by eye is a morning's work you'd never actually schedule.

blocks.body: Every rented shop platform has an opinion about how you should sell, and you spend the first year working around it. The counter and the website draw down the same stock, orders from every channel land in one queue, the money side knows what things cost. So you can ask what you earned last month and get an answer.

When it breaks on a Saturday, I get the call. Send me your product list and a few days later you get a private link to your own shop with your own products in it, plus an audit of everything broken in your catalogue. hero.role: Pavlo Kostiuk — drone & ground control software
hero.title: Ground control software for ArduPilot and PX4 drones
hero.intro: I founded Aircast: a Raspberry Pi unit on the drone that streams video and MAVLink over 4G or Starlink, and a QGroundControl fork on the ground that flies it. This page is the engineering record — what was built, measured and flown, with the public code to read.

hero.label: glass-to-glass video from the drone to the operator over 4G or Starlink

ledger.note: Measured on the Aircast beta: H.264 encoded on the Raspberry Pi, carried by WebRTC, drawn in the ground station.

rest.label: one QGroundControl fork — Android, iOS, macOS, Linux, Windows — plus the core running in a browser
flight logs from real and simulated flights, kept and replayable
Android CPU for the telemetry pump after the core rewrite; video now zero-copy

gcs.title: Ground control station
gcs.intro: Aircast ships a QGroundControl fork for every platform. Half of each native head turned out to be logic written twice, so the core is moving to Rust behind a C ABI — the heads only render.
bullets: Rust core runs in a browser worker and flies a vehicle; missions and raw-socket links are still native-only
Android: the core re-did everything every 100 ms and video went GPU → CPU → GPU. Pump 79% → 1–2% of a core, video zero-copy, a 720p flight at ~61% on a OnePlus 6
Device pages are a JSON API drawn natively in each app's Device tab — transport, forms, charts, setup wizard and joystick wording live in the core once
Windows 11 head designed in Fluent: 53 screens covering every macOS view on a 48 px rail
Phone simulator rehearses a whole mission by the drone's own parameters: DO items, terrain, failsafes, wind, GPS and motor faults — SITL is kept for real flight code and feel

shot.title: The iOS head flying an Auto mission
shot.alt: Aircast iOS ground station in Auto mode flying waypoint 5 of 8 over a city map with the route drawn
shot.body: Native SwiftUI head over the shared core: mission progress, waypoints and the link status drawn from the same state every other platform uses.

telemetry.title: Telemetry, video and protocols
telemetry.intro: The unit on the drone speaks MAVLink to the flight controller and to any ground station, and turns one camera into every stream a client might want.
bullets: MAVLink routed from the autopilot to a public UDP endpoint, so QGroundControl or Mission Planner connect from anywhere
RTSP camera advertised over MAVLink; the ground station finds the stream without typing a URL
One camera → RTSP, WebRTC, HLS and SRT from a Go media engine; WebRTC SFU for multi-viewer
TypeScript MAVLink toolkit: types generated from the XML dialects plus a real-time message parser — public
Own NTRIP caster (v1 and v2) feeding RTK corrections from a Leica base into the ground station
Starlink dish client over the real SpaceX gRPC protocol, with a fake dish for tests without hardware

shot.title: Live video with the on-board OSD
shot.alt: Live FBWA video from a fixed-wing drone at 56 km/h with altitude, distance from home, 4G link bitrate and battery overlaid
shot.body: A real flight over the Alazani valley: altitude, speed, distance from home, 4G link at 3.2 Mbit/s and battery voltage burned into the stream by the unit on the drone.

missions.title: Missions and payloads
missions.intro: Flight features are proven in SITL against the autopilot's own commands before a real drone carries them.
bullets: Four-bay payload drop in sequence — by hand and from a mission; ArduPilot has one gripper, so each bay gets its own servo via DO_SET_SERVO
Auto-intercept drop on a moving car: release uses the target's real velocity and re-aims every second
Grab / hold-to-release on the camera page sends DO_GRIPPER and shows the flight controller's ack
Tap-to-aim on the SIYI ZR30 gimbal: tap the video, the camera points there — accuracy measured and corrected
Loiter's 1.5 s speed time constant made the sticks feel wooden; cut to ~1 s in a parameter file the real drone loads too

shot.title: A nine-waypoint mission across the ridge
shot.alt: Ground station map with a nine-waypoint mission over mountains and the live camera feed in a corner
shot.body: Auto mode at 155 m with the camera feed picture-in-picture; the route was planned on the phone and flown by the autopilot.

hardware.title: Hardware, gimbals and the bench
hardware.intro: Everything is checked on a hardware-in-the-loop bench before it meets a propeller.
bullets: CUAV-X7 bench: the autopilot runs SimOnHardWare, is flashed through the on-drone daemon, and flies a 10 m takeoff and landing with real video — 5 of 5
Found and fixed the daemon dying for good on a probed serial port hang-up (SIGHUP)
A real drone's stored tune on the simulated frame caused a ±5 m weave on go-to; the bench now resets to firmware defaults before every flight (±0.5 m)
Viewpro and Topotek gimbal cameras bridged to MAVLink as Go libraries; SIYI ZR30 driven natively
RadioMaster AX12 radio and Starlink client readiness checked and documented

shot.title: Synthetic view over real terrain
shot.alt: Synthetic 3D camera view of a city rendered from real terrain and building data, loitering at 80 m
shot.body: The simulated camera renders the real ground and buildings, so the bench and the phone simulator rehearse over the same terrain the drone will see.

device.title: The unit on the drone
device.intro: A single Go daemon on a Raspberry Pi: video, telemetry, network and updates, with the apps drawing its API.
bullets: Raspberry Pi OS image built with pi-gen; flasher writes a card with Wi-Fi, hostname, SSH key and VPN key in about 10 minutes
A/B OTA updates, so a bad release never bricks a card in the field

Opt-in LUKS2 encrypted data partition unlocked by Clevis from a Tang server or a per-card cloud key — a VM boot harness and the first real Zero 2 W cards each caught bugs that would have locked every card out
Per-device HTTPS: Let's Encrypt certs under a computed-DNS domain, because Cloudflare's free tier caps records at 200
Cellular modem, interface priority and failover, data budget with alerts, all from the browser

shot.title: Flasher: Wi-Fi and hostname written to the card
shot.alt: Aircast Flasher customisation step with Wi-Fi network, password and hostname fields
shot.body: Step three of four: the card leaves the laptop already knowing its network and its name on it.
